meta.methodology: Read framework.md, torah_119_packages.json, torah_119_additions.json, torah_119_ce_edges.json, and torah_119.txt. Collected all node IDs already assigned to packages (including additions). Extracted all unique node IDs from cause/effect edges. Identified nodes appearing in CE edges but not in any package. Assigned each unassigned node to a package by its ESSENTIAL NATURE — the core concept it represents — considering polarity (good/evil/neutral).

assignments.reason: בְּשַׁבָּת ('on Shabbat') is the locative/temporal form of שַׁבָּת. Its essential nature IS Shabbat — the temporal vessel of daas. The prefix בְּ (in/on) does not change its core identity. It belongs in Package 1 alongside שַׁבָּת because it refers to the same concept: the Shabbat context in which daas flows to every person. In the eitza edge (id 756), בְּשַׁבָּת → דַּעַת expresses the directional flow: being in the state of Shabbat causes daas to be drawn down. The node's essential nature is Shabbat itself.

רַחֲמָנוּת (compassion as a character trait/attribute) is the central concept of the mercy domain in Torah #119. The Rebbe states: 'מִדַּת הָרַחֲמָנוּת תָּלוּי בְּדַעַת' — the trait of compassion depends on daas. Its essential nature is MERCY — the positive moral quality that flows from knowledge. It is not daas itself (which is the cognitive/spiritual faculty), but rather its fruit in the domain of interpersonal conduct. It is explicitly named as the opposite of כַּעַס (anger). Its polarity is good — it belongs to the domain of holiness and right conduct.

רַחֲמִים (mercy/compassion) is what the sick person needs — 'כְּשֶׁאָדָם צָרִיךְ לְרַחֲמִים'. Its essential nature is mercy in its broadest sense — the divine and human quality of compassion. It is functionally synonymous with רַחֲמָנוּת in this Torah's framework, differing only in grammatical form (רַחֲמִים = the mercy one receives/needs; רַחֲמָנוּת = the trait of being merciful). Both belong to the same compassion domain.

This node describes the ACT of showing mercy on another — 'הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹלֵחַ לוֹ רַחֲמָנוּת, שֶׁהוּא יְרַחֵם עַל אַחֵר'. Its essential nature is compassionate action toward others. God sends a person the capacity for mercy so that he will show mercy to another. This is the active expression of רַחֲמָנוּת — mercy in practice. It belongs in the compassion package as a specific manifestation of the mercy trait.

This node — 'that he should have compassion on others' — expresses the same essential nature as שֶׁהוּא יְרַחֵם עַל אַחֵר but from the perspective of the sick person's obligation. The Rebbe concludes: 'צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ רַחֲמִים עַל אֲחֵרִים, וְזֶה תָּלוּי בְּדַעַת'. Its essential nature is having/exercising compassion. It is the prerequisite condition for receiving heavenly mercy. It is mercy directed outward, firmly in the compassion domain.

מְרַחֲמִין עָלָיו ('they have mercy on him') is the reciprocal heavenly response: 'כָּל הַמְרַחֵם עַל הַבְּרִיּוֹת מְרַחֲמִין עָלָיו'. Its essential nature is receiving mercy from Heaven — the divine compassion that mirrors human compassion. Though it is the EFFECT (receiving mercy) rather than the CAUSE (giving mercy), its core concept is still mercy/compassion — the same domain as רַחֲמָנוּת and רַחֲמִים, just from the receptive side. Polarity is good: this is heavenly compassion flowing to the person.

new_packages.label: רַחֲמִים
new_packages.reason: Torah #119's eitza chain flows from Package 1 (שַׁבָּת/דַּעַת) into a distinct conceptual domain: compassion/mercy. The five compassion nodes — רַחֲמָנוּת, רַחֲמִים, שֶׁהוּא יְרַחֵם עַל אַחֵר, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ רַחֲמִים עַל אֲחֵרִים, מְרַחֲמִין עָלָיו — all share the ESSENTIAL NATURE of mercy. They are not aspects of knowledge (daas) or Shabbat; they are the moral-practical fruit of daas. The Torah's argument is precisely that daas PRODUCES compassion (eitza), not that daas IS compassion (bechina). Therefore these nodes form a separate thematic cluster. The dominant node is רַחֲמָנוּת, which the Rebbe names as the midda (trait) and from which all specific expressions derive. This package is 'good' — compassion belongs to the domain of holiness.

stats.eitza_flow_summary: Package 1 (שַׁבָּת וְדַעַת) →eitza→ Package 2 (רַחֲמִים): Shabbat/daas produces and enables compassion. The full chain: בְּשַׁבָּת → דַּעַת → רַחֲמָנוּת / שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ רַחֲמִים עַל אֲחֵרִים → מְרַחֲמִין עָלָיו. This captures the Torah's core practical teaching: Shabbat grants daas, daas enables compassion, compassion toward others brings heavenly mercy upon oneself.
